geo.label: hold / data dependent
parts: Macro Stance

The US data flow is cooling while the Fed debate tilts toward a December cut [[n3758]]. The Beige Book pointed to a cooling labour market and softer spending ahead of the December rate decision [[n3747]]. ADP showed private payroll losses accelerating over four weeks [[n3577]], while weekly jobless claims fell to a seven-month low [[n3579]]. Consumer confidence fell by the most since April as job worries grew [[n3560]]. The October CPI release was cancelled [[n3492]] and the BEA dropped its advance Q3 GDP estimate [[n3525]], so the Fed is deciding with less inflation data than usual.
Rates & Curve

The 2-year Treasury closed the prior session at 3.47% and the 10-year at 4.02%, a 10Y-2Y spread of 55 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-11-28). Over 20 observations the 2-year is down 12 bps and the 10-year down 6 bps, so the spread is up 6 bps; over five observations both are down 8 bps. The 3-month bill sits at 3.88%, which leaves the 10Y-3M spread at 14 bps, and the 30-year is at 4.67%, 65 bps over the 10-year (US Treasury, prior close 2025-11-28). The curve is positively sloped but still flat by historical standards (long-run average about +90 to +100 bps), and the 20-observation move is a bull steepening (both down, 2Y down more); the writer’s reading is that the market is pricing a cut rather than a growth scare. The S&P 500 closed at 6,849.09, up 4.75% over five sessions but only 0.39% over 20, and the VIX at 16.35 is down 0.56 points over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28).
New / Most Important

The most important item is who runs the Fed: Trump says he has made his choice to lead the Federal Reserve [[n3850]], with five finalists named [[n3835]] and Kevin Hassett reported as the favourite [[n3746]]. Investors see a Hassett-led Fed as a risk to the dollar [[n3778]], and the dollar was set for its biggest weekly fall in four months as the Fed focus sharpened [[n3794]]. The Fed’s own split is showing up in rate options hedging [[n3763]]. The 20-session change in the dollar index is only down 0.07% at 99.46 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28), so the currency has not yet re-priced the cut. Gold touched a six-week high on the same cut bets while silver hit a record [[n3851]].
Playbook ✓

Stay neutral on duration until the December decision and the chair pick are known. Buy the 2-year for the cut case, and hold a smaller 10-year position as the hedge against a hawkish chair signal, because the 10-year has only moved 6 bps over 20 observations. Equities need confirmation: the S&P 500 is up 4.75% over five sessions but barely changed over 20, so add exposure only if the gain holds into the decision. The consensus anchor is the 7,500 year-end 2026 call from JPMorgan [[n3780]] and HSBC [[n3783]], which argues for buying dips rather than chasing. What would change the call is a Fed chair signal that puts the cut in doubt, which would push the 2-year higher and the dollar up.

geo.label: benign / rate cuts muted
parts: Macro Stance

Euro-area growth and inflation are on a benign path, which keeps rate-cut bets muted [[n1197]]. The ECB has told euro-zone banks to prepare for the risk of a dollar squeeze [[n1192]], a reminder that the funding side of the banking system depends on US conditions. Lagarde has warned that the EU is missing the boat on AI [[n1160]]. The IMF says Germany’s mid-term prospects are constrained even as Chancellor Merz sees signs the economy is turning [[n1187]], and it says higher government spending alone will not fix Germany [[n1188]]. The UK’s growth forecasts were lowered from next year [[n1191]].
Credit & Inflation

Euro-area inflation is easing, but the feed gives two levels that do not line up: October came in at 2.1% [[n1119]], and a headline dated 20 November has inflation down to 2.5% [[n1146]]. The November PMI shows euro-zone business activity growing steadily [[n1154]]. The banking item that matters is the Morningstar analysis of which European banks are most exposed to US tariff risk [[n1177]], together with the ECB warning on dollar funding [[n1192]]. Market levels confirm a calm backdrop: EUR/USD closed at 1.1600 and is up 0.24% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28), and the Stoxx Europe 600 closed at 576.43, up 0.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). The DAX is down 0.51% over the same window, which the writer reads as the broad index not yet pricing a rebound.
New / Most Important

The EU spending review has produced a list of winners and losers [[n1174]], and the Commission is preparing a plan to cut raw-materials reliance on China, which Reuters describes as slow [[n0612]]. European defence stocks and gas prices fell as the US and Ukraine made progress on a peace plan [[n1166]], and an earlier defence-stock rally was described as crumbling on the same talks [[n1165]]. The FT asks who killed Europe’s single-market dream [[n1209]], which is the structural question behind the cautious equity tone.
Playbook ✓

Mixed. Keep German cyclicals at benchmark weight: the autos rally is already in the price, with BMW up 9.07% and Volkswagen up 9.04% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28), and the IMF caveat limits the upside. Prefer the broad STOXX 600 over single-country banks until the tariff exposure in the banks is clearer. Add euro-dollar exposure only if the Fed chair pick points to a weaker dollar, because the ECB has flagged a dollar squeeze risk. The trigger to turn constructive is a fresh euro-zone growth print that beats the current benign reading; the trigger to turn defensive is a euro-bank funding headline.

geo.label: targeted support / weak demand
parts: Macro Stance

China’s domestic demand is weak and the policy response is targeted rather than broad. The factory data are soft: the AP reports China’s factory activity contracting for an eighth month in November despite the trade truce [[n3842]]. The property and credit data are weaker still, with new bank loans falling sharply in October and missing forecasts [[n0293]]. The government is responding with consumption measures rather than a large credit push: a 19-point plan names “hotspot” sectors to spur consumption [[n0518]]. The Chinese equity market is down over 20 sessions, which the writer reads as the market’s verdict on that response.
PMIs & Activity

The latest factory reading in the feed is November: the AP reports China’s factory activity contracting for an eighth month in November despite the trade truce [[n3842]], and Bloomberg describes the factory slump as the longest stretch on record [[n0589]]. A private survey was read two ways: CNBC reported the November factory gauge unexpectedly contracting and missing estimates [[n0603]], while a second CNBC headline said activity edged up but stayed in contraction as holiday demand faded [[n0601]]. Those headlines conflict on the direction, so the clean read is that manufacturing remains in contraction, with services the weaker leg. Industrial profits fell in October after two months of strong growth [[n0498]], although a China Daily headline describes steady growth in industrial profits over the first 10 months [[n0533]].
Credit Impulse

The latest credit print in the feed is October. New bank loans fell sharply and missed the forecast [[n0293]], and the Bloomberg read is that China saw its worst credit growth in a year as demand dried up [[n0295]]. The WSJ reports the worst investment decline in years as the slowdown continued [[n0316]]. The feed carries no November credit print, so the next data release is the test. The policy signal is to let credit slow: Goldman sees a longer easing pause after the PBOC changed its mind on policy [[n0271]], and the central bank’s confidence messaging has raised the question of whether rate cuts are on the back burner [[n0281]].
Property

Property is still deteriorating, with official prices falling at the fastest pace in a year in October [[n0317]], and a Bloomberg headline says the home-price slump deepened as stimulus failed to halt the slide [[n0307]]. CNBC described housing weakness intensifying alongside falling investment [[n0297]]. The developer Vanke is the stress point: it sought a first extension on an onshore bond payment, and the bonds slumped [[n0458]], then the bonds plunged on a plan to delay repayment [[n0531]]. Vanke also pledged its entire stake in its management unit to a state backer [[n0596]], which the writer reads as state support rather than a market solution. UBS’s property optimist retreated to a deeper slump call [[n0405]].
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Fiscal policy is aimed at consumption and high-tech industries rather than housing. The 19-point plan names hotspot sectors [[n0518]], and China’s planning agency warned of too many robots in the economy [[n0556]]. The trade picture is calmer: the US extended tariff exclusions on some Chinese industrial goods as part of the trade truce [[n0501]], and Trump says he will visit China in April after a call with Xi [[n0414]]. The yuan is firmer, with China setting its strongest yuan fix in over a year as Fed-cut bets rise [[n3768]]. The writer’s reading is that currency strength is a policy tool rather than a growth signal, which limits the room for the PBOC to cut rates aggressively.
Markets & Flows

The Hang Seng closed at 25,858.89, down 0.18% over 20 sessions, and the Shanghai Composite at 3,888.60 is down 1.67% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). The CSI 300 ETF ASHR is down 2.83% over 20 sessions at 32.58, the FXI large-cap ETF is down 1.54% at 39.53, and the internet ETF KWEB is down 6.59% at 37.57 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). USD/CNY closed at 7.0758 and is down 0.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). Flows point to state support: national-team-tied ETFs were among the most bought in the selloff [[n0430]], and JPMorgan upgraded China’s stocks on several positive drivers [[n0549]].
New / Most Important

The most important new item is the crackdown on crypto. The PBOC vowed a crackdown on virtual currency and flagged stablecoin concerns [[n0585]], and Hong Kong stablecoin stocks slumped on the warning [[n0599]]. The writer’s reading is that the PBOC is tightening the perimeter around crypto rather than easing. The PBOC is also pushing yuan borrowing abroad to internationalise the currency [[n0257]], and IMF researchers flagged currency risks as nations swap dollar loans into yuan [[n0272]]. This is the policy thread to watch alongside the property stress.
Playbook ✓

Bearish on domestic cyclicals and property. Avoid developers and the onshore bond market until Vanke’s repayment path is clear, and keep banks at underweight while credit growth is at a one-year low. Keep a tactical position in internet and China AI names, because the sector’s valuation is still below US peers and Goldman argues the rally has room [[n0433]], but size it for a drawdown, since KWEB is down 6.59% over 20 sessions. The trigger to add is a credit print that stops falling; the trigger to exit is a further property price drop in the next release. ⚠ Divergence: JPMorgan’s upgrade of China equities [[n0549]] and the national-team buying [[n0430]] point up, while most macro prints point down; the exception is the China Daily headline that industrial profits recorded steady growth over the first 10 months [[n0533]].

geo.label: hike bias / fiscal expansion
parts: Macro Stance

The Bank of Japan is leaning toward another hike. Governor Ueda sent a clear hint at a chance of a December rate hike [[n1776]], and Noguchi has advocated gradual increases [[n1704]]. Tokyo core inflation has brought the BOJ closer to a hike [[n1726]]. The fiscal side is expansionary: the government finalised a $117 billion extra budget mostly funded by debt [[n1728]], and Japan is issuing $75 billion in new bonds to fund the stimulus [[n1738]], with more short-term debt to fund Takaichi’s stimulus [[n1756]]. The result is a central bank tightening into a looser fiscal stance, which is the tension the yen is trading.
Activity & Currency

USD/JPY closed at 156.2840 and is up 1.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). A Reuters headline says the dollar eased against the yen as the BOJ hinted at a hike [[n1777]], and a Morning Bid note says the rate-hike prospect arrested the yen’s decline, for now [[n0618]]. Japan’s finance minister says FX moves are not based on fundamentals [[n1764]]. Activity is mixed: capex growth slowed to 2.9% in Q3 but pointed to resilient demand [[n1783]], and the manufacturing PMI decline slowed in November [[n1210]]. The Nikkei 225 closed at 50,253.91, down 2.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28).
Playbook ✓

Mixed. Buy yen on dips only if the December hike is confirmed; a hike with the 156 level holding would argue for a short USD/JPY position with a tight stop. Keep Japanese equity exposure in AI memory and capex names, since Micron’s $9.6 billion investment in western Japan [[n1773]] is a concrete capex signal, and hedge the currency sensitivity of the broad Nikkei. The trigger to turn bearish on the yen is a BOJ decision that is not followed by a hike; the trigger to turn bullish is a weaker dollar after the US chair decision.

Bearish on rate-sensitive domestic equities and mildly bearish on the Aussie dollar. Prefer the resource and buyback-light names that are less exposed to a housing slowdown. The trigger that would change the call is the next monthly CPI read coming in below the October overshoot; the trigger to press the view is a Reserve Bank signal that a May move is live.

Silver is at a record [[n3811]] and gold is closing in on its record high [[n3812]], while the broad materials index is up only 3.75%. The writer’s reading is that the precious-metal move is a rates and dollar trade, not an industrial-growth trade, so it does not confirm a cyclical recovery.
Narrative

Real estate is trading on the rate-cut bets and a softer mortgage rate. XLRE closed at 41.67 and is up 1.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). Mortgage rates dropped during the week on signs of a weaker job market [[n3766]], which is the rate channel for property.
Reported

The feed carries no REIT earnings in the window. The housing evidence is weak: more than half of US homes have dropped in value over the last year [[n3515]], and Zillow removed climate-risk scores from home listings [[n3624]].
EPS Upside Watch
Mortgage-sensitive REITs are the set-up if the December cut comes through. The upside depends on the rate path, not on operating results.
⚡ Breaking Convention
Real estate is rising while more than half of homes have lost value over the year. The writer’s reading is that the sector is priced on rates, and the housing data do not yet support the move.
Narrative

Utilities are split between regulated and merchant power. XLU closed at 45.31 and is up 1.01% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). NextEra is up 5.70% at 86.29 over 20 sessions, while Constellation at 364.36 is down 4.74% and Vistra at 178.86 is down 5.72% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). Investors are being pulled into yield: boomers are flocking to utilities for yields above 6% [[n3817]].
Reported
The feed has no fresh utility earnings in the window. Barron’s argues Dominion Energy is a utility play with AI upside and a buy [[n1089]], which is the bull view of the power-demand story.
EPS Upside Watch
Merchant power names are the set-up if AI load keeps growing. Dominion is the regulated-with-AI-optionality name that the Barron’s note points to [[n1089]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The AI-power names are falling while the regulated name is rising, which cuts against the consensus that AI load lifts all utilities. The writer’s reading is that the market is discounting merchant power margins.
Narrative

European autos are being priced on China. The iShares STOXX Europe 600 Automobiles ETF closed at 46.44 and is up 2.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28), while BMW is up 9.07% and Volkswagen up 9.04% over the same window. The consensus is that German makers are earning a lot in China [[n0333]], but the China EV profit squeeze is the counter-driver [[n0552]].
Reported

The feed gives no European auto earnings in the window. A Stellantis headline puts the policy risk in the sector: its chairman warns the European car industry risks “irreversible decline” because of CO2 targets [[n2419]].
EPS Upside Watch

Volkswagen can now build EVs in China and claims costs can fall by up to 50% [[n0460]], which is the set-up for a cost surprise in 2026. Volkswagen plans to export Chinese-made cars to more overseas markets but rules out Europe [[n2421]], so the writer’s reading is that the cost gain stays in China-built volume.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The auto ETF is up over 20 sessions even with China EV profit headlines pointing down [[n0565]]. The writer’s reading is that the market is pricing cost cuts from local production, not the China volume, which cuts against the bear view.
Narrative

US–Asia semiconductors are the core AI supply chain and have lagged the broad market over 20 sessions. SOXX closed at 296.74 and is down 2.84% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28), with TSMC down 3.86%, ASML down 1.44%, and Micron up 5.57% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). Micron will invest $9.6 billion in western Japan to make AI memory chips [[n1773]].
Reported

Nvidia’s Q3 forecasts topped estimates with AI-chip sales described as off the charts [[n0935]], and Rapidus denied a 1.4nm fab timeline amid Japan’s chip push [[n1732]]. The reported read is strong forecasts that did not lift the group.
EPS Upside Watch

Memory and networking names are the set-up: Broadcom is up 7.04% over 20 sessions and up 16.19% over five at 402.96 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28), and Micron is up 17.44% over five sessions. The feed gives no dated print for either.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Nvidia is down 12.76% over 20 sessions despite a strong forecast, while Broadcom and Micron are rising. The writer’s reading is that the market is rotating inside the chip group toward memory and custom silicon, away from the single-name leader.

earnings_pattern.title: Raised outlooks were paid, cost and spend were punished
parts: Rewarded

The clearest reward went to raised outlooks in consumer names. Abercrombie shares soared 33% after earnings [[n1058]], Kohl’s rallied on a forecast raise [[n1057]], and Best Buy raised its annual forecasts as shoppers snapped up holiday deals [[n1055]]. Burlington raised its outlook as low-income shoppers stayed resilient [[n1056]], and Dell rose on earnings after a supposed disaster [[n1072]]. Alibaba shares rose as AI drove a 34% jump in cloud sales [[n1044]].
Punished

Workday posted a lukewarm subscription revenue and its shares fell [[n1045]]. Li Auto missed on revenue [[n1087]], and J.M. Smucker forecast annual profit below estimates [[n1069]]. Meituan posted its first loss in three years as the food-delivery war raged [[n1112]]. Alibaba’s profit plunged 72% on its costly foray into instant retail [[n1062]], and Alibaba’s AI arm surged even though big spending hit profit [[n1050]]. Pets at Home’s profit dive prompted a call for urgent action [[n1077]].
Pattern

The market pays for a raised outlook with visible demand and punishes spending that delays profit. The consumer names that raised guidance were rewarded in size, with moves of 33% to 37% in Abercrombie [[n1058]] [[n1059]]. The Alibaba read shows the split inside one report: cloud growth rewarded, instant-retail spend punished. The writer’s reading is that investors treat spend without a payback date as a cost, not an investment. Nvidia’s post-earnings reaction was also split, with headlines reporting both a slide and a rise [[n0935]] [[n0944]], so the pattern is not uniform across AI names.
Attention into EPS

The next wave of attention is on banks and software. Banks head into the fourth quarter priced for perfection [[n1104]], the Visible Alpha breakdown of Canadian big banks’ Q4 expectations is the reference point [[n1102]], and costs are climbing on higher pay [[n1103]]. Credo Technology is one of the names with a Q2 earnings release ahead, which the feed frames as a buy, sell or hold question [[n1101]]. The writer’s reading is that the outlook, not the quarter, sets the bar in this window.
Playbook

Own the names that raised outlooks on visible volume, and avoid those whose beat depends on spend without a payback. Treat the next Canadian bank print and the Credo release as the test of whether the market still pays for beats. The trigger to add to consumer discretionary is a second raise in the holiday window; the trigger to reduce is a guidance cut from a name that already raised, which would show the rewarded pattern reversing.

underowned.title: US gas-to-power as the AI load fuel
parts: Attention Gap

The writer’s reading is that gas is being overlooked as the marginal fuel for AI power demand, and that coverage focuses on the AI chips rather than on the power that runs them. Henry Hub natural gas closed at 4.85, up 22.6% over 20 sessions and up 6.41% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). Barron’s makes the utility-AI case for Dominion [[n1089]], and a Yahoo Finance headline projects that US data-center electricity demand will triple [[n2789]].
Exposure & Risk

The exposure is the gas producers and the power names that buy gas, such as NextEra at 86.29 (up 5.70% over 20 sessions) and Constellation at 364.36 (down 4.74%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). The risk is that the gas spike is weather-driven and reverses, and that the merchant power names have already fallen on the same theme.
Trigger to Watch

The trigger is a cold-weather gas print that holds the Henry Hub level, or a utility earnings call that quantifies AI load. Without a dated print the theme stays underowned, and the writer’s reading is that it becomes consensus only after a power contract is announced.

underowned.title: Copper as the grid and AI data-centre metal
parts: Attention Gap

The exposure is the copper miners and the grid-equipment names, but the feed gives no positioning data. The risk is that copper is traded for dollar and rates moves as much as for demand, and an Australian energy-challenge headline argues that power supply could derail AI data-centre build-outs [[n0082]].

The trigger is a data-centre power contract that names copper-intensive build-outs. Until then the theme stays off the consensus list, and the writer’s reading is that the first clear grid-capex order would move it into consensus.

The trigger is the Rapidus timeline or a Micron Japan production milestone. The feed gives no date, so the writer’s reading is that the theme stays underowned until the first volume-production headline.

underowned.title: European defence after the peace-talk fade
parts: Attention Gap

Poland will receive $51 billion from the EU defence programme [[n1833]], which is the budget support the price does not reflect.

The exposure is European primes and the Polish-linked suppliers. The risk is a peace deal that lowers the defence budget case, since the headlines are already trading on the peace track. The feed gives no positioning data for the names.

crypto.title: Bitcoin’s worst run, and the ETF flows that turned
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 90,394.31 on the prior completed daily close 2025-11-30, down 14.72% over 20 sessions from 105,996.59 and up 3.49% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-11-30). Bitcoin is 28% below its record high [[n0780]], and November was the second-worst month of 2025 [[n0791]].
New / Most Important

The most important new item is the ETF flow turn. Bitcoin funds were set for their worst month as investors pulled $3.5 billion [[n0621]], and BlackRock’s iShares bitcoin fund saw a record exodus [[n0622]]. Spot bitcoin and ether ETFs then recovered momentum with their first net-positive inflow week since October [[n0783]]. Strategy’s index status is the structural risk: MSCI is considering removing it over its bitcoin exposure [[n0685]], and Jim Chanos closed his MSTR short [[n0721]]. Nasdaq is seeking a higher trading cap for options on the top bitcoin ETF [[n0741]].
Playbook

Mixed. Buy bitcoin only on a confirmed run of net ETF inflows, because one positive week after a $3.5 billion outflow month is not yet a trend. Avoid Strategy while MSCI’s review of its index status is pending, since the card shows MSTR down 30.4% and the index review is a binary event. The trigger to turn positive is a second week of ETF inflows with bitcoin holding above its 20-session reference; the trigger to turn defensive is a MSCI decision to remove Strategy from its indexes. The writer’s reading is that size should stay small until MSCI settles its pending review.

flows.title: Liquidity is being set by the Fed-cut and BOJ-hike bets
parts: Global Liquidity

Liquidity is being set by two central banks moving in opposite directions. The Fed is priced toward a December cut, with the Beige Book describing a cooling labour market ahead of the December decision [[n3747]], and the dollar was set for its worst week since July as the Fed rate cut looms [[n3798]]. A BeInCrypto headline from 30 November says the Fed ends quantitative tightening the next day [[n1326]], so the balance-sheet runoff is set to stop. The BOJ is leaning toward a hike, with Ueda’s hint at a December move [[n1776]]. The IMF has flagged currency risks as countries swap dollar loans into yuan [[n0272]], which is the non-US liquidity channel to watch.
Rates & Dollar

The US curve is bull steepening: the 2-year closed at 3.47% and the 10-year at 4.02%, with the 2-year down 12 bps over 20 observations and the 10-year down 6 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-11-28). The dollar index at 99.46 is down 0.07% over 20 sessions and down 0.70% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). The writer’s reading is that the short end is pricing the cut and the long end has not followed: IEF at 97.50 is up 0.71% over 20 sessions while TLT at 90.21 is down 0.39% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28).
Credit Check

Index-level credit is calm in the card: HYG closed at 80.99, up 0.24% over 20 sessions, and LQD at 111.86 is up 0.16% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). The writer’s reading is that the stress sits in specific names and AI issuance: Big Tech’s AI debt wave is threatening to swamp credit markets [[n1218]], UBS credit funds could face a 10% write-down over First Brands [[n1261]], and a Vanke bond plunge on a repayment delay [[n0531]] sits in the China developer book. The HYG and LQD tape is therefore not confirming the China property and Chinese developer stress, which is the gap to watch.
Equity & Fund Flows

Fund flows are concentrated in crypto and in the index effect. Over half of hedge funds now hold crypto, which the industry calls a turning point [[n0742]], and Cathie Wood’s ARK loaded up on Google, Coinbase, Circle and bitcoin ETF shares [[n0723]]. SanDisk joined the S&P 500 and the index effect lifted its shares [[n3804]]. In Australia, a buyback boom is signalling dividend pain for investors [[n0070]], and European active funds show a sign of life [[n1178]]. On the broad market, US equity funds saw their first weekly outflow in six weeks [[n1311]].
Portfolio Implication

Be long the front end and the belly for the cut case, and keep a hedge in the 10-year because the long end has moved only 6 bps over 20 observations. In FX, keep the yen short only with a hedge into the BOJ decision. In crypto, size bitcoin exposure to the ETF-flow trigger rather than the price. Credit is not confirming the China stress, so the position in Chinese developers and the index credit are the two books to keep separate.

anticipatory.title: Fed chair pick and the December cut
parts: What Is Priced

The market is pricing a December cut and a dovish chair. The Beige Book pointed to a cooling labour market ahead of the December rate decision [[n3747]], and JPMorgan shifted its outlook on a Fed cut to December [[n3760]]. Trump says he has made his choice to lead the Fed [[n3850]], with Kevin Hassett reported as the favourite [[n3746]]. The 2-year is at 3.47% and has fallen 12 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-11-28).
Conditional Expression

If the chair pick is Hassett and the cut comes, the dollar falls further and gold keeps its climb, so add to gold and to the 2-year. If the pick or the decision is hawkish, the dollar rallies from its worst-week low [[n3798]] and the front end sells off, so the 2-year and the dollar long are the trades to reverse.
Risk

The risk is the inflation data. The CPI release was cancelled [[n3492]] and the FT is asking how sticky inflation is [[n3623]], so a hot inflation print after the decision could reverse the cut pricing faster than the feed shows.

anticipatory.title: BOJ hike and the yen
parts: What Is Priced

The market is pricing a December BOJ hike. Ueda sent a clear hint at a chance of a December rate hike [[n1776]], and the dollar eased against the yen on the hint [[n1777]]. The Tokyo core inflation print brought the BOJ closer to a hike [[n1726]]. USD/JPY at 156.2840 is up 1.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28).
Conditional Expression

If the BOJ hikes, the yen rallies and USD/JPY falls, so the short-yen position is the trade to close and the Nikkei exporters are the names to trim. If the BOJ holds, the yen extends its decline, so keep the short-yen hedge and add to Japanese capex names.
Risk

The risk is that the government’s extra budget and the debt-funded stimulus [[n1728]] keep the yen weak even after a hike, since the FinMin says FX moves are not based on fundamentals [[n1764]]. USD/JPY is already up 1.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28), so the writer’s reading is that a hike alone may not reverse the yen’s trend.

anticipatory.title: China property and the Vanke test
parts: What Is Priced

The Hang Seng is down 0.18% over 20 sessions at 25,858.89 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28).
Conditional Expression

If Vanke secures a state-backed repayment path, the China developer bonds rally and the Hang Seng property names lead, so add to onshore credit selectively. If the repayment is delayed further, the developer bonds slump and the PBOC’s rate-cut pause [[n0271]] holds, so stay underweight banks and property.
Risk

The risk is a policy signal that the consumption plan [[n0518]] is enough. The PBOC’s confidence messaging [[n0281]] suggests no rate cut is imminent, so a fast move in property prices would depend on a broader stimulus that the feed does not show.

anticipatory.title: MSCI decision on Strategy

Conditional Expression

If MSCI removes Strategy, passive selling follows and MSTR falls further, so the put spread ahead of the review is the trade. If MSCI keeps it, the shares can rebound toward 254.57, MSTR’s close 20 sessions earlier, so the call spread is the trade. Either way, size the position to the event.
Risk

The risk is that Strategy’s bitcoin exposure is a bet on the ETF flow turn, so a positive ETF week could lift MSTR even if the index decision goes against it. Margin-call risk is also in the headlines [[n0775]].

retail_intro: Kohl's brings the meme-stock comeback into an earnings test, echoing the familiar gap between GameStop-style identification and a retailer's operating recovery.

retail.title: Kohl's / KSS — “the comeback has an earnings receipt”
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Kohl's offers a more tangible version of the comeback trade than a stock rising solely because a crowd has found it. Business Insider described the meme-stock favourite surging again and explicitly distinguished the move from Reddit hype. [[n1060]] The attraction is that the believer can now point to an operating development, rather than only to the persistence of other holders. A familiar retailer is easy to understand, a damaged reputation leaves room for improvement, and an outlook increase allows an owner to imagine that the business has crossed a turning point. That is a powerful invitation to reassess a stock which many investors may have stopped following.
What Is Driving It

Reuters linked the share rally to another forecast increase and described signs that the turnaround was taking hold. The Wall Street Journal also reported shares rising as the retailer lifted its outlook. [[n1037]] [[n1057]] Those are the developments that distinguish this selection from a generic hunt for a short squeeze. Better guidance changes the earnings discussion; a rising share price changes the willingness of previously indifferent investors to hear it. The next question is whether the improvement can survive ordinary trading conditions. A forecast increase can support a rerating, but the entry price still determines how much further improvement a buyer needs.
The Social Signal

The attention evidence is unusually useful because the headline identifies both the meme identity and the business improvement. Business Insider's framing supplies the link between a popular stock narrative and the company's latest announcement. [[n1060]] It does not require an invented message count or a claim that every retail investor has become bullish. The crowd's appealing interpretation is that sceptics are using an outdated description of the company. The less comfortable interpretation is that an earnings surprise has briefly brought different types of buyers into the same trade. Momentum buyers, turnaround investors and devoted holders can agree on direction while having very different reasons to sell.
Historical Analog

GameStop's earlier transformation into a retail identity provides the behavioural analogy, although it does not establish that Kohl's will follow the same price path. The first stage is recognition: an ordinary shop becomes an investable symbol of a comeback. The next stage arrives when the rising share price itself attracts participants who have little interest in the operating detail. An earnings catalyst can make that second wave more durable, because holders have a commercial argument to repeat. It can also obscure the difference between a business becoming better and its shares remaining attractively priced after investors have noticed the improvement.
Smart Money View

An institutional buyer can take the raised outlook seriously while insisting on evidence that the recovery is repeatable. The supportive view is that management's improvement is reaching the forecast and deserves a fresh valuation. The cautious view asks what has to happen to demand, costs and cash generation for that valuation to remain justified. A short seller may reduce exposure because the operating surprise invalidates part of the original thesis, without accepting the crowd's most optimistic destination. Prefer a measured turnaround position to treating every favourable earnings headline as confirmation of a permanent change in the company's competitive standing. The quality of the recovery also matters: a company that improves through repeat customer demand deserves a different assessment from one benefiting mainly from a temporary reduction in expectations. The next operating update should help distinguish those paths.
When the Narrative Breaks

The narrative weakens if the next operating update fails to support the higher outlook, or if favourable company news repeatedly stops producing a resilient price response. Those tests concern the business and the market's expectations, rather than a prediction that online enthusiasm must disappear. Add only after the initial excitement allows the valuation and execution requirements to be assessed. Take partial profits if a modest turnaround position becomes a concentrated bet through appreciation. Avoid leverage built around the assumption that a squeeze will arrive on demand. A comeback earns additional capital when its operating evidence improves; the affection of existing holders is not a substitute for that improvement.

retail.title: Strategy / MSTR — “the leveraged bitcoin proxy”
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Retail sees Strategy as a way to own bitcoin with leverage through the equity. The stock is down 30.4% over 20 sessions, which the crowd reads as a buying opportunity, and Fundstrat’s Tom Lee says bitcoin could hit new highs by year-end [[n0697]]. The crowd treats the drawdown as the entry point. The Motley Fool’s pitch that buying bitcoin today could 10x a net worth [[n0793]] is the same story at retail scale.
Where It Breaks

The trigger is MSCI’s pending review of the index removal [[n0685]]. The instrument risk is that a removal forces passive selling, and the put spread ahead of the review captures it. Jim Chanos closed his MSTR short [[n0721]], which the writer reads as the short crowd stepping back. A failed bitcoin rebound after the first ETF inflow week [[n0783]] would confirm the drawdown for retail, and bitcoin is already down 14.72% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-11-30).

retail.title: Eli Lilly / LLY — “the trillion-dollar pill”
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Retail sees Lilly as the obesity winner that has crossed a trillion dollars. The valuation milestone is a headline [[n0993]], and the card shows the stock up 27.35% over 20 sessions at 1,075.47 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-11-28). The crowd’s view is that the weight-loss demand is the durable story. The Fierce Pharma note that Lilly stepped up as vaccine sales declined [[n1026]] is the crowd’s proof point.
Where It Breaks

The trigger is a guidance cut or a slowdown in weight-loss demand. The instrument risk is the 27% run, which leaves the shares exposed to a single print. A break below 844.50, Lilly’s close 20 sessions earlier, would tell retail the trade has ended.
